content_signals.reader_job: inspect evidence chain and release decision

reader_job.statement: Inspect the evidence chain, production boundary, and release decision.
reader_job.scenario: Review a source-backed offline HTML deck before reuse.

design_decisions.visual_thesis: Evidence before style: make the production chain inspectable through distinct semantic layouts.
design_decisions.content_tension: A structural fixture can pass while a production deck still needs decisions, rhythm, evidence, and review.
design_decisions.selected_direction: Use one registered Swiss system to sequence evidence, exact data, risk, and decision close.

rejected_directions.reason: The lighter template was recorded as rejected; no stronger historical rationale is claimed.
A long-form report would not match the sequential presentation reader job.

design_decisions.restraint_rule: Use one Swiss visual system, keep the secondary accent marker-only, and forbid visible text inside generated SVG assets.
design_decisions.method_note: This is a retrospective classification of the artifact, not evidence that the original build used the current Taste Contract.

reusable_rules: Vary visual weight by semantic role while staying inside one registered system.
Bind layout inventory, source mapping, calculations, media declarations, and target-surface captures.
Use a risk/control page and decision close when the reader must inspect release readiness.
anti_patterns: Treating a structural fixture as proof of production quality.
Forcing long-form report reading into a sequential deck rhythm.
Reusing the system when calculation provenance or media truth is incomplete.
reuse_boundary: Do not reuse as proof of native PPTX, PDF, Figma, live-data, or external-fact capability.
Do not reuse the visual system when the current reader job or content topology differs materially.

non_claims: This record does not claim real-user comprehension, satisfaction, business impact, or universal template fit.
The retrospective does not claim that the current Taste Contract was used during the original build.
This record does not prove native export fidelity or external source verification.
